jsonFormatter.metaDescription: Format, validate, and minify JSON online for free. Your text stays in the browser by default.
jsonFormatter.title: JSON Formatter
jsonFormatter.intro: Paste JSON to beautify it, catch syntax errors, or shrink file size before you send or save it. Processing happens locally in your browser.
jsonFormatter.howBody: Paste raw JSON and press Format for readable indentation or Minify to remove whitespace. Invalid documents surface a parser error so you can fix typos quickly.

uuidGenerator.metaDescription: Generate random UUID v4 identifiers in bulk—secure random values for IDs and everyday use.
uuidGenerator.title: UUID Generator
uuidGenerator.intro: Create version 4 UUIDs using your browser's secure random source. Copy a single value or generate a batch for seed data.
uuidGenerator.howBody: Set the quantity (1–100) and press Generate. Each run creates fresh v4 UUIDs you can use for unique IDs, invites, or sample data.

base64.metaDescription: Encode text or binary strings to Base64 and decode safely with UTF-8 support.
base64.title: Base64 Encode / Decode
base64.intro: Use Base64 for data URLs, HTTP headers, and quick sharing of short payloads. All transformations run locally in your browser.
base64.howBody: Type or paste on the left and encode, or paste Base64 on the right and decode. The helper uses UTF-8 so emoji and non-Latin scripts round-trip correctly.

timestamp.metaDescription: Convert Unix seconds, milliseconds, and ISO-8601 timestamps with local and UTC views.
timestamp.title: Timestamp Converter
timestamp.intro: Switch between numeric timestamps and readable dates when you work with app or website data. Everything is calculated locally.
timestamp.label: Unix seconds, Unix ms, or ISO-8601
timestamp.howBody: Paste a 10-digit Unix time in seconds, a 13-digit millisecond value, or a full ISO string such as 2026-04-04T12:00:00Z. The table updates instantly with equivalent representations.

jwt.metaDescription: Decode JWT headers and payloads for debugging. This tool does not verify signatures or secrets.
jwt.title: JWT Decoder
jwt.intro: Inspect JSON Web Tokens without sending them to a server. Decoding is for troubleshooting only—never treat output as trusted without signature verification.
jwt.label: JWT string
jwt.errorSegments: A JWT needs at least header and payload segments.
jwt.safetyBody: This page only decodes the encoded parts of the token. It does not check signatures, expiration, or who issued it. Always verify tokens with your app's own security checks before trusting them.

timeZone.metaDescription: Compare local times across regions and convert one moment between two places, with daylight saving handled.
timeZone.title: Time Zone Converter
timeZone.intro: Plan meetings across regions with daylight saving handled for you. Pick two places by time zone and compare the same moment side by side.
timeZone.labelDt: Local datetime (interpreted in your browser zone)
timeZone.invalid: Pick a valid date and time.
timeZone.howBody: Pick a date and time, then choose two time zones by name. You will see the same moment in both places, including summer/winter clock changes, without doing the math yourself.

dateCalculator.metaDescription: Add or subtract days from a date and measure the difference between two calendar dates.
dateCalculator.title: Date Calculator
dateCalculator.intro: Plan sprints, contracts, and shipping windows using clear day-based math. Calculations use your browser clock and plain calendar dates (no time-of-day).
dateCalculator.span: Span: {days} full calendar days between the two dates.
dateCalculator.howBody: Pick two dates to see how many full calendar days sit between them. In the second panel, nudge a base date forward or backward by any integer number of days—handy for SLA and trial expirations.

ageCalculator.metaDescription: Calculate exact age in years, months, and days from a birth date through today or a custom date.
ageCalculator.title: Age Calculator
ageCalculator.intro: Answer how old someone is on a specific day using calendar-aware math. Useful for forms, games, and compliance checks.
ageCalculator.error: Choose a birth date on or before the reference date.
ageCalculator.howBody: Select a birth date and the day you want to measure against—defaults to today. The output breaks the span into whole years, months, and days without rolling everything into decimal years.

imageCompressor.metaDescription: Compress JPG, PNG, and WebP images in the browser before upload. Optional max width and quality controls.
imageCompressor.title: Image Compressor
imageCompressor.intro: Shrink photos for email attachments or faster web uploads. Files stay on-device; we never persist your originals.
imageCompressor.errorSize: Each image must be smaller than {mb}MB.
imageCompressor.errorCompress: Compression failed. Try a different image or settings.
imageCompressor.howBody: Tune quality and maximum size, then choose an image under 10MB. Preview the result and download when it looks right—compression runs in the background so the page stays responsive.

pdfMerge.metaDescription: Merge multiple PDF documents into a single file. Uploads are processed on the server only for the duration of the request.
pdfMerge.title: PDF Merge
pdfMerge.intro: Combine reports or scanned pages in the order you select. Avoid uploading confidential PDFs if you require zero server-side handling.
pdfMerge.limits: You can merge up to 8 files, up to 12MB each, 40MB combined.
pdfMerge.howBody: Multi-select PDFs in the order you need. We stitch them server-side and trigger a download. Encrypted or owner-locked PDFs may be rejected.

regexTester.metaDescription: Test JavaScript regular expressions with custom flags. See matches and capture groups instantly in your browser.
regexTester.title: Regex Tester
regexTester.intro: Experiment with patterns against sample text. Everything runs locally—nothing is uploaded.
regexTester.howBody: Enter a JavaScript-style pattern, toggle flags, and paste text to test. Invalid patterns show an error; valid patterns list each match index and captured groups when present.

diffChecker.metaDescription: Compare two versions of text side by side with line-level highlights for additions and deletions.
diffChecker.title: Text Diff
diffChecker.intro: Paste an older and a newer version to see what changed. Useful for configs, drafts, and logs.
diffChecker.howBody: Paste text into both boxes. Added lines appear on a green background; removed lines on a soft red background. Unchanged lines stay neutral.

jsonToCsv.metaTitle: JSON to CSV Converter Online Free
jsonToCsv.metaDescription: Convert a JSON array of objects to CSV in your browser. Headers are built from all keys found in the rows.
jsonToCsv.title: JSON to CSV
jsonToCsv.intro: Turn API-style JSON into a table you can open in Excel or Google Sheets. Only flat object fields are supported—nested objects stay as JSON strings if you stringify them first.
jsonToCsv.errorShape: Expected an array of objects (or a single object).
jsonToCsv.howBody: Provide a JSON array where each item is an object with string or number fields. Keys become column headers; missing fields become empty cells.

cronGenerator.metaDescription: Compose five-field cron schedules and preview the next run times. Runs entirely in your browser.
cronGenerator.title: Cron Expression Helper
cronGenerator.intro: Edit minute, hour, day, month, and weekday fields, or start from a preset. Preview helps sanity-check before you paste into crontab or a scheduler.
cronGenerator.copyHint: Standard five-field order: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week
cronGenerator.howBody: Cron syntax varies slightly by system; this helper follows a common five-field pattern. Use presets as a starting point, then tweak fields. Preview lists the next few upcoming times in your local timezone.

markdownPreview.metaDescription: Write Markdown with GitHub-style tables and task lists, with live preview; export a PDF that matches the preview when the PDF service is configured.
markdownPreview.title: Markdown Preview
markdownPreview.intro: Draft notes, readme snippets, or documentation with instant feedback. Rendering uses GitHub Flavored Markdown features such as tables and strikethrough. PDF export sends your Markdown through this site’s server to a dedicated converter; content is not kept by the tool after the file is generated.
markdownPreview.pdfErrorGeneric: Export failed. Try again later or check server configuration.
markdownPreview.pdfHint: Download a PDF that matches the preview (requires the PDF worker and PDF_SERVICE_URL).
markdownPreview.howBody: Use Source, Preview, or Split to focus on editing, reading the render, or seeing both. Split uses two columns on large screens and stacks on small ones. Fullscreen keeps the same layout options in a full-screen workspace (press Esc or Exit to close). PDF export uses the same rendering rules as the preview; if the converter is not configured, use your browser’s print-to-PDF instead.

loanCalculator.metaDescription: Estimate fixed-rate loan monthly payment, total repayment, and total interest. For planning only—not financial advice.
loanCalculator.title: Loan Payment Calculator
loanCalculator.intro: Enter principal, annual interest rate, and loan length. Results use a standard amortizing loan formula. Verify numbers with your lender before making decisions.
loanCalculator.invalid: Enter positive numbers for amount, a non-negative rate, and a term greater than zero.
loanCalculator.howBody: Use your quoted APR and full loan term. The calculator assumes monthly compounding in line with common consumer loan estimates. Rounding may differ slightly from your bank's system.

roiCalculator.metaDescription: Calculate return on investment percentage from starting and ending values. Handy for quick checks before deeper analysis.
roiCalculator.title: ROI Calculator
roiCalculator.intro: ROI here means (ending value − starting value) ÷ starting value, shown as a percentage. Starting value must be greater than zero.
roiCalculator.invalid: Starting value must be a positive number. Ending value can be any number.
roiCalculator.howBody: Enter what you put in and what it is worth now (or at exit). Positive ROI means growth; negative means a loss versus the starting amount.
